rationale: The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by measured CI workflow evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, evidence_scope measured_ci_workflow_on_fork) showing 26.8% elapsed savings from adding an explicit job timeout. The repository's CI history shows repeated successful runs, providing representative duration history for setting budgets. The workflow currently relies on GitHub's default 360-minute job timeout, so a hung job can consume up to 6 hours of runner time. Adding timeout-minutes to every job bounds runaway consumption without changing any build or test command, preserving all required checks and coverage. Timeouts are set with operational headroom: 30 minutes for most jobs, 60 minutes for jobs that install cross or run many cargo commands (features_check, cross-targets, cross-tests). This adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or new network access.
